title: Warm Spinach Chicken Salad
seoTitle: Warm Spinach Chicken Salad | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sliced chicken over wilted spinach with bacon vinaigrette for ten
subtitle: Sliced chicken over wilted spinach with bacon vinaigrette for ten
description: Chicken thighs roast and slice, then serve over lightly wilted spinach with warm bacon-mustard vinaigrette, sliced mushrooms, and hard-boiled egg. Hearty enough for a cold-night shift.

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.instruction: Season thighs with salt and olive oil. Roast at 425°F on a sheet pan 25–30 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F. Rest and slice. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Cook bacon and mushrooms
steps.instruction: Render bacon in a skillet until crisp. Remove and chop. Sauté mushrooms in bacon fat 6–8 minutes until golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Build warm vinaigrette
steps.instruction: Whisk vinegar, mustard, and shallot into warm bacon fat off heat. Crumble half the bacon into the dressing.

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.instruction: Toss spinach in a large bowl with warm dressing until leaves just wilt—about 30 seconds of gentle tossing.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.instruction: Top wilted spinach with sliced chicken, mushrooms, egg quarters, and remaining bacon crumbles. Serve immediately.

proTips: Baby spinach handles warm dressing better than mature spinach leaves.
Add sliced red grapes for sweet contrast if your crew likes fruit in salad.
This does not hold—plate to order or assemble in small batches.
tonightSpread: Warm spinach salad plated with crusty rolls on the side.
Roasted sweet potato wedges for crew who want more carbs.
leftovers: Slice cold chicken for sandwiches with leftover bacon.
Use wilted spinach in a frittata the next morning.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Warm salad sounds fancy but it is just smart hall cooking—hot dressing wilts spinach slightly and makes the plate feel like dinner, not diet food.
mealPrepNotes: Render bacon slowly for best vinaigrette fat. Dress spinach lightly at service—too much and it collapses. Mushrooms sauté just before plating.
